lineage: Rebrand of DarkSide (Jul 2021); announced shutdown Nov 2021, with operators/ExMatter tooling reappearing in ALPHV/BlackCat
summary: BlackMatter emerged in July 2021 as a DarkSide rebrand, run by the group Symantec tracks as Coreid, and attacked US critical infrastructure including food and agriculture. Affiliates used embedded, previously compromised credentials, LDAP/SMB AD discovery and remote encryption over admin shares, plus a Linux encryptor for ESXi. A custom .NET exfiltration tool, ExMatter, stole selected documents over SFTP/WebDAV before encryption, and backups were wiped rather than encrypted.
uniqueTraits: Encryptor ships with embedded compromised credentials and uses LDAP/SMB to find and encrypt every reachable host and share
Custom ExMatter .NET exfiltration tool (SFTP, WebDAV fallback) that self-deletes
CMSTPLUA COM-interface UAC bypass inherited from DarkSide
Wipes/reformats backup stores and encrypts ESXi with a Linux variant
